newsitem.title: UK: Turkey central bank gold holdings 119 T in Oct 1996.
newsitem.headline: Turkey central bank gold holdings 119 T in Oct 1996.

text.p: The gold holdings of the Central Bank of Turkey rose to 119 tonnes as of last month from 116.5 tonnes at the end of last year, the bank's assistant general manager, Ayse Botan Berker, told a conference on Tuesday.
Gold holdings represent about 7.65 percent of total reserves, or $1.4 billion, Berker said in comments prepared for delivery at the City of London Fifth Central Banking Conference.
By contrast, the population of Turkey was estimated to hold gold worth $50-$75 billion, she said.

Despite the small increase in the bank's gold holdings, the share of gold in total reserves fell below 10 percent this year for the first time as foreign exchange reserves hit all-time highs, Berker said.

"In 1990 the share of gold in total was 19.7 percent whereas the Forex holdings were $6 billion," she said. "The share of the gold in the Central Bank balance sheet has also decreased to 5.0 percent in October 1996 from 6.6 percent in 1990."
The ratio of gold to reserves for all central banks is currently at about 23 percent when valued at market prices, and drops to 10.7 percent with the official rate, she said.
At market prices, total gold reserves make up 30.1 percent of total reserves in industrial countries and 15.3 percent for all developing countries, she added.
Despite gold's declining share in Turkey's total reserves, the dollar value of gold has held steady in recent years, coming in at $1.5 billion in 1990, Berker said.

"It is the central bank's strategy to hold the gold reserves stable," she said. "In an environment where there is increasing mobility in central banks' gold holdings, our gold can be considered dormant."
Twenty tonnes of the bank's gold holdings were held in depository financial institutions, she added.
